scope: 8,293 published questions still missing item-level source and curriculum-objective metadata
purpose: A reviewed source map for the next metadata batches. Track-level links are evidence candidates, not proof that every question has already been checked.
rules: Do not copy a track-level link into a question until the prompt, options, answer and explanation have been checked against that source.
Use a specific curriculum objective or exam-board statement; do not use a generic topic title as an objective.
Keep legacy questions published only while the content review proceeds; never mark them approved from this map alone.

sources.title: National curriculum mathematics programmes of study

gcse-maths.objectiveMethod: Map each topic and item to the relevant mathematics programme-of-study statement before applying metadata.

gcse-english-language.objectiveMethod: Map reading, writing, spoken-language and grammar items to the applicable GCSE English Language subject-content statement.

gcse-english-literature.objectiveMethod: Map each text, language/form and context item to the selected exam-board specification; do not infer a set text from a topic label alone.

gcse-history.objectiveMethod: Record the selected exam-board period, event and historical-enquiry objective for each item.

gcse-computer-science.objectiveMethod: Map computational thinking, programming, systems, data representation, networks and security items to the relevant GCSE Computer Science subject-content statement.

gcse-geography.objectiveMethod: Map each item to the selected exam-board physical, human or geographical-skills statement.

ai-for-everyone.objectiveMethod: Map introductory concepts, responsible use and AI ethics to the UNESCO AI competency framework; keep general claims clearly educational and non-official.

business-english.objectiveMethod: Approve a business-English scope and map each item to a specific workplace communication objective; the generic functional-skills link is only a candidate source.
